title: Age of Mythology: Extended Edition
notes: A side note in case it helps others: in Highball, the graphics mode is per environment, so Steam games sharing an environment share one mode. I keep this environment on DXMT for AoM and switch to "Apple's DirectX 12 support" for The Witcher 3 (#1213).
session: Played 20 min (random map) through Highball with the fix. Without it, every session crashed within 6 min.
issues: Crashes to desktop after roughly 4–6 minutes of a random-map game. This follows up on #1196, which was rated 5 after an 11-minute session that was too short to hit the problem. The Highball log shows hundreds of these right before the crash, followed by the game closing: On one run the game's own `Logs/<session>/startup.txt` also recorded `EXCEPTION CAUGHT: Access Violation ... read at 0x0`. Cause: `AoMX.exe` is 32-bit and is **not** marked large-address-aware (PE characteristics `0x102`), so it is limited to 2 GB of address space. Longer or bigger matches run out. What I tried: | Engine | Renderer | Result | |---|---|---| | x64-crossover26.3-r31 | d3dmetal | OOM crash after about 4 min | | x64-crossover26.3-r31 | dxmt | OOM crash after about 5 min | | x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28 | dxmt | OOM crash after about 6 min | | x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r28 (services stuck on wined3d after an engine switch) | wined3d | `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` assert after about 30 s | | **x64-crossover26.3-r31 + `WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1`** | **dxmt** | **20 min random map, 0 OOM errors, normal shutdown** | **Fix:** use engine x64-crossover26.3-r31 and set the environment variable `WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1`. Highball's launch log confirms it: "it runs with WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1 and the game wants 1". The r28 engine's ntdll doesn't contain this variable, so it only works on the CrossOver engine. What not to do: setting the large-address-aware bit in `AoMX.exe` itself works for memory, but Steam then reports "signature verification failed for file aomx.exe", marks the app as Files Corrupt, and stops it launching. The env var avoids touching the binary. Suggestion: it might be worth having the recipe or database entry set `WINE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1` (and the CrossOver engine) for this game automatically. Other 32-bit, non-LAA titles may hit the same thing.
